behavioral: e2e pc mode auto-derives ROI from milmb markers
The bulk runner's pc leg was 0/17: scripts/run_e2e.sh invokes
tests/e2e.sh as `TRIGGER_MODE=pc FIXTURE=...` with no ROI_START/ROI_END,
and the per-fixture default boundary symbols (_hybrid_enter_pc /
_hybrid_exit_pc) were removed long ago, so every pc-mode fixture failed
at arg-resolution with "ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set". CSR
mode (17/17) proved the round-trip logic itself was fine.

Fix: when a caller leaves BOTH ROI vars unset, e2e.sh now derives them
from the fixture's milmb ROI markers via objdump:
  ENTER = entry marker  csrwi milmb,0  (enc 7c005073)
  EXIT  = LAST exit marker csrwi milmb,1 (enc 7c00d073)
The marker PCs are passed verbatim: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
(--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
(compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so the marker PC reproduces CSR
mode's switch points exactly. EXIT takes the LAST marker so rt_pc_jump,
which jumps over 15 poison csrwi milmb,1 to its real exit at
phase_b_landing, resolves to the reachable marker rather than the first
dead one. Encodings are unambiguous (csr 0x7c0, uimm 0/1), so the
raw-bytes match needs no CSR-name table from objdump.

Derivation lives in a new pure helper roi_markers_from_disasm (roi.sh),
unit-tested in roi.test.sh (in-order, jump-over-poison, no-marker cases).
roi_resolve_pair is unchanged, so its required-vars contract and the
./hsim run --mode pc CLI (which always passes explicit --pc-start/
--pc-end, never hitting the fallback) are untouched.

Tests: full e2e MODE=both now 35/35 (pc 17/17); roi.test.sh,
test_kernel_cycles.sh (explicit-boundary pc), and
test_hsim_run_pc_required.sh all pass.
